transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, October 2. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Sundar Pichai on Google launching Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model yet. Google has unveiled Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model yet, topping 13 of 18 benchmarks against OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. The model targets coding, legal, finance and cybersecurity work, with a 1 million token output limit. It is rolling out first to cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program, with paid API users and Google AI Ultra subscribers next in line. Wife gets late husband's job, leaves in-laws; HC orders 25 percent salary for mother-in-law. In this case, a widow secured a government job under this provision but later allegedly left her late husband's parents on their own. The Rajasthan High Court explained that a compassionate appointment is intended to provide monetary support to a family struggling to cope with the sudden death of its sole earning member. Ukraine claims first combat use of its home-made ballistic missile against Russia. In a significant escalation of the conflict, Ukraine has confirmed its inaugural deployment of the FP-7 tactical ballistic missile, a cutting-edge weapon designed by Fire Point. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed this news on October 1 via Telegram. While details regarding the missile's target and effects are currently classified, the FP-7 boasts an impressive range of about 250 kilometers. 'He has good ideas': Putin lauds PM Modi's peace push to end Russia-Ukraine war. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday lauded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's efforts to seek an end to the Ukraine conflict, saying that he has "good ideas" for achieving a peaceful resolution. 10,500-year-old wood found 20m deep in Germany's Lake Arendsee. Archaeologists have recovered remarkably preserved worked wood dating back 10,500 years from beneath Germany's Lake Arendsee. The finds include a 1.6-metre post with felling marks and split boards up to 1.3 metres long. Researchers believe they may be remnants of Mesolithic huts or previously unknown structures, offering new insights into hunter-gatherer life. Saudi hands Omani flydubai pilot to UAE; Trump vows 'hitting hard' if Iran links found. The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a flydubai flight and attempting to take control of the aircraft has been handed over by Saudi Arabia to the United Arab Emirates. Family moves 255-year-old mansion 50 miles by barge across Chesapeake Bay. A 255-year-old mansion, Galloway House, was moved by a Maryland family to prevent it from being demolished. The structure traveled approximately 50 miles across the Chesapeake Bay after extensive planning and specialized equipment. Crews lifted the 400-ton house for a phased relocation that began in September 2019. After arriving at its new waterfront property in Queenstown, restoration efforts commenced to preserve its historic character. US energy department engineer arrested for allegedly helping Iran-backed Houthis. A US department of energy electrical engineer has been arrested for allegedly providing material support to the Iran-backed Houthi rebels. SC judges decline to meet parliamentary panel on one-nation, one-election. The Supreme Court has declined to meet the parliamentary committee, which is examining a Constitution amendment bill proposing simultaneous elections, saying it will not be desirable for senior judges to discuss the matter as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review. 100-year Massachusetts family farm preserved in 120-acre conservation deal. In a significant move towards sustainability, over 120 acres of Hoyt Farm in Essex have been shielded from commercial development, safeguarding its agricultural, forestry, and wildlife heritage. With cultivation practices dating back two centuries, this initiative, driven by local leaders and state agencies, secures essential natural resources and bolsters community food security, all while optimizing financial support to minimize town burden. 'If India won a medal, we owe it to her': Captain Swayams on Savitha's heroics. Welcome to TimesofIndia.com's interview series looking back at India's medal-winning campaigns at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand. After kicking things off with Srinath Narayanan and India's silver-winning Open team, we turn to Swayams Mishra, captain of the bronze-winning women's team. In an exclusive interaction, the 34-year-old opens up about his first full stint as captain, the difficult decision-making around Vaishali, Savitha Shri's match-winning impact, and much more.
